investigation.summary:
SHIELD_WorldSystem::update (lines 1933-2323) contains 5 O(N) passes over all loaded chunks. Analysis reveals:

**Pass 1 (lines 1952-1972): Initial state-count scan**
- READS: m_streaming_state.chunks (chunk states, mesh vertex/index counts)
- WRITES: m_last_streaming_budget_stats (ready_chunks, renderable_chunks, idle_chunks, loading_chunks, meshing_chunks)
- TYPE: Pure telemetry (zero functional impact)
- SKIPPABLE: YES — only populates stats, never used for control flow

**Pass 2 (lines 2027-2038): Meshed_columns unordered_map build**
- READS: m_streaming_state.chunks (mesh_vertices, mesh_indices, current_lod, chunk coords)
- WRITES: meshed_columns (local vector, ~O(N) alloc + fill)
- TYPE: Functional (enables Pass 3 seam-crack detection)
- SKIPPABLE: PARTIAL — only needed if any chunk has stale transition faces (checked by missing_transition_faces logic at 2112-2114). On a static settled world where all chunks were meshed in prior frames, this could be skipped if no missing_transition_faces conditions exist.

**Pass 3 (lines 2067-2164): Meshing-candidate loop + sort**
- READS: m_streaming_state.chunks (chunk state, pending_lod, coords, mesh data, applied_transition_faces)
- WRITES: meshing_candidates vector (per-chunk distance/LOD evaluation, dispatch_meshing_jobs at 2241)
- TYPE: Functional (identifies chunks needing remesh)
- SKIPPABLE: NO — determines which chunks dispatch meshing. On a static world with no movement or dirty chunks, this still scans all N chunks to find zero work (scan-and-find-nothing scenario).

**Pass 4 (lines 2247-2260): Physics-collider scan**
- READS: m_streaming_state.chunks (chunk state, has_collision, current_lod, mesh data)
- WRITES: physics_system (collision via replace_chunk_collision)
- TYPE: Functional but throttled
- SKIPPABLE: NO — incremental collision creation. Already throttled by MAX_COLLISION_MESHES_PER_FRAME; on a static world scans all chunks to find (typically) zero work.

**Pass 5 (lines 2264-2282): Final state-count scan**
- READS: m_streaming_state.chunks (same as Pass 1)
- WRITES: m_last_streaming_budget_stats (ready_chunks, renderable_chunks, idle_chunks, loading_chunks, meshing_chunks) — reset then repopulated
- TYPE: Pure telemetry (zero functional impact)
- SKIPPABLE: YES — duplicate of Pass 1, only for telemetry

**Key findings for static-world optimization:**
- Passes 1 & 5 are REDUNDANT telemetry scans (clear_streaming_state_counts + full re-count twice)
- Pass 3 scans all chunks even when anchor is unmoved and no chunk is dirty (no early-exit gate)
- Pass 2 rebuild is unnecessary if meshed_columns didn't change
- Passes 3 & 4 do meaningful work (determine meshing/collision assignments) but scan entire set even when zero work exists
- update_chunk_activation (line 1991) is already throttled (m_update_tick_counter), which gates the REAL work (activation/eviction); the per-frame passes happen every frame
- Determinism risk: Any optimization that gates scans must NOT affect world_hash or replay equivalence (m_last_streaming_budget_stats is telemetry-only and excluded from hashing)
key_facts: Pass 1 (lines 1953-1972): State-count scan into m_last_streaming_budget_stats — pure telemetry, iterates all chunks to count ready/renderable/idle/loading/meshing states
Pass 2 (lines 2027-2038): Builds meshed_columns unordered_map by scanning chunks with mesh data, stores (chunk_y, lod) per horizontal column for seam-crack detection

Pass 3 (lines 2067-2164): O(N) meshing-candidate loop over all chunks. For each: checks pending_lod, computes closest_anchor distance, evaluates required_lod, checks for missing_transition_faces, conditionally pushes to meshing_candidates. Then sorts candidates (lines 2202-2216) and dispatches up to meshing_budget chunks

Pass 4 (lines 2247-2260): O(N) collision scan over all chunks. For each Ready chunk at LOD0 with mesh data but no collision: calls replace_chunk_collision, incremented until MAX_COLLISION_MESHES_PER_FRAME (throttled)
Pass 5 (lines 2264-2282): Identical state-count scan to Pass 1. Calls clear_streaming_state_counts (line 2263) then re-counts all chunks into m_last_streaming_budget_stats

Mutations: Pass 1/5 write m_last_streaming_budget_stats (telemetry). Pass 2 writes local meshed_columns (consumed by Pass 3). Pass 3 writes meshing_candidates vector (fed to dispatch_meshing_jobs). Pass 4 writes physics_system collision state (functional)
Telemetry: m_last_streaming_budget_stats is read-only for telemetry queries (get_last_streaming_budget_stats). Never fed into world_hash or determinism-critical logic
update_chunk_activation (line 1991) guarded by m_update_tick_counter >= STREAMING_ACTIVATION_INTERVAL_FRAMES (decoupled, throttled). Passes 1-5 run EVERY frame unthrottled

Static world behavior: When anchor unmoved and all chunks Ready/meshed: Pass 1 counts N chunks (no work). Pass 2 rebuilds meshed_columns from N chunks (no change). Pass 3 scans N chunks, missing_transition_faces finds no work, meshing_candidates stays empty. Pass 4 scans N chunks, all have has_collision==true, zero work. Pass 5 counts N chunks (same as Pass 1)
risks: Determinism gate: m_last_streaming_budget_stats is pure telemetry (never hashed, never feeds control flow). Optimizing Passes 1/5 is safe. But any gate on Passes 2-4 MUST preserve the same scheduling decisions (meshing_candidates, physics_system state) across replay

Anchor movement detection: Gating Passes 2-4 on 'anchor unchanged AND all chunks not dirty' requires tracking prior anchor position. If a chunk becomes dirty mid-frame (e.g., from external edit), the gate must re-enable scanning. The current code has NO chunk-dirty flag; adding one requires careful initialization

Seam-crack false negatives: Pass 2 (meshed_columns) feeds missing_transition_faces logic (line 2043-2062). If a finer chunk arrives AFTER a coarse chunk was meshed, missing_transition_faces detects the stale skirt and queues a remesh. If Pass 2 is skipped when meshed_columns 'hasn't changed', but a new mesh was uploaded in the render pipeline between frame N-1 and N, the comparison is out-of-phase and could miss a stale skirt (low probability but non-zero edge case)

Physics throttle interaction: Pass 4 is already throttled per-frame (MAX_COLLISION_MESHES_PER_FRAME). Gating the loop early could cause collision to fall behind meshing if many chunks arrive at once. However, the current loop breaks immediately after MAX limit, so skipping the entire loop on a static world saves N-max iterations of no-op reads

World_hash replay: If the optimization uses anchor_moved as a gate (e.g., 'if anchor didn't move, skip Passes 2-4'), this is deterministic and replay-safe because anchor_positions are replayed identically. But HeadlessServerTick and other gates must see the SAME meshing_candidates output (if zero) across both paths (unoptimized vs optimized)

Telemetry miscount: Skipping Pass 5 means m_last_streaming_budget_stats becomes stale. Any frame-to-frame telemetry delta would be wrong. If telemetry is wired into UI/logs, users see a flat/frozen frame count. Solution: keep Pass 5 or gate it differently

investigation.summary:
The 5 redundant O(N) per-frame streaming passes in SHIELD_WorldSystem::update (lines 1933-2284) split into determinism-sensitive vs render-only:

DETERMINISM-SENSITIVE (world_hash-affecting):
1. Pass 3 (lines 2011-2242): meshing-candidate loop and dispatch_meshing_jobs. The dispatched jobs populate chunk.mesh_vertices and chunk.mesh_indices, which ARE hashed in world_hash (ChunkToJson lines 240-241 serialize them). Changing WHEN meshing completes or which chunks are meshed changes the hashed state on the next ComputeWorldHash call (server waits for streaming jobs before hashing).

2. Pass 4 (lines 2245-2260): physics-collider scan and replace_chunk_collision. Sets chunk.has_collision=true, which IS in world_hash (ChunkToJson line 248). Changing WHEN collision is created affects world_hash timing, but the collision state itself is deterministic post-creation.

RENDER/TELEMETRY-ONLY (world_hash-independent):
1. Pass 1 (lines 1945-1972): state-count scan updating m_last_streaming_budget_stats. Purely telemetry, no chunk modification.

2. Pass 2 (lines 2025-2038): meshed_columns unordered_map build. Read-only structure for seam-skirt detection, does not modify hashed fields.

3. Pass 5 (lines 2264-2283): final state-count scan. Purely telemetry.

SERVER DETERMINISM DISCIPLINE: ServerWorldRunner::RunFixedTicks (lines 384-394) calls world_system->update then wait_for_streaming_jobs, ensuring all generation/meshing is quiesced before the next tick. ComputeWorldHash (lines 415-437) snapshots AFTER wait_for_streaming_jobs, guaranteeing hashed state reflects completed work.

CRITICAL: mesh_vertices/indices and has_collision APPEAR in world_hash because they are (1) in PersistedFields() and (2) serialized by ChunkToJson. An optimization to gate passes 1,2,5 on anchor movement would be safe, but passes 3,4 cannot be gated without flagging the change.

design.design:
Make the per-frame streaming work in SHIELD_WorldSystem::update (the multi-anchor overload, SHIELD_WorldSystem.cpp:1933) collapse to near-zero on a static, fully-settled world via a single cheap "streaming dirty" guard derived ENTIRELY from deterministic inputs (anchor positions + chunk-state transitions), plus two structural cleanups (dedup the twin telemetry scans; track collision-needing chunks in a small set instead of scanning all chunks).

Core principle for determinism: passes 3 (meshing dispatch) and 4 (collision creation) mutate fields that ARE in world_hash (mesh_vertices/mesh_indices at WorldPersistenceRoundtrip.cpp:240-241, has_collision at :248). The server (ServerWorldRunner.cpp:385-394) calls update() then wait_for_streaming_jobs() before ComputeWorldHash, so the hash always reflects the quiesced result of whatever was dispatched THIS update. Therefore the elision gate is replay-safe IFF it is a pure function of replayed inputs: (a) anchor_positions (replayed bit-identically), and (b) the chunk-collection state which evolves deterministically from those inputs. It must NEVER depend on wall-clock, render-thread mesh uploads, frame timing, or anything excluded from the snapshot. The gate is frame-local and is itself NEVER serialized/hashed.

THE GUARD (compute once at top of update, after process_completed_meshing_jobs):
  bool streaming_dirty =
        anchor_moved(anchor_positions)            // any anchor crossed a cheap chunk-cell threshold vs m_last_anchor_positions, or the anchor count changed
     || m_streaming_state.dirty_generation != m_last_serviced_generation  // a chunk transitioned Ready / was added / removed / edited since we last fully serviced
     || meshing_jobs_active()                     // jobs in flight: results must be applied + may seed follow-on remeshes
     || has_active_job(m_streaming_state.generation_job_handle)
     || m_update_tick_counter + 1 >= STREAMING_ACTIVATION_INTERVAL_FRAMES; // the activation tick is due this frame (keep activation cadence exactly as today)

When !streaming_dirty: skip passes 2, 3 (candidate build/sort/dispatch) and the body of pass 4 (collision scan). Still ALWAYS run: m_update_tick_counter++ , water-system update (it is NOT part of the gate per the existing comment that it must see the current chunk list), and a single telemetry refresh (see cleanup B). When streaming_dirty: run the full path exactly as today, and at the end set m_last_serviced_generation = m_streaming_state.dirty_generation and m_last_anchor_positions = anchor_positions.

m_streaming_state.dirty_generation is a uint64_t bumped at the deterministic transition points: chunk Ready transition in process_completed_meshing_jobs (SHIELD_WorldSystem.cpp:3703/3705/3707), synchronous Ready in EnsureSurfaceReadyNear (:2702), chunk insert (:2651, :3451, :3816), chunk erase (:2596), and voxel edit / has_collision invalidation. Because every input to passes 2-4 (chunk set membership, per-chunk state, current_lod, mesh presence, water/transition flags) changes ONLY through these points, a generation bump conservatively covers every case that could change pass-2/3/4 output. The counter is incremented in the SAME deterministic order in run and replay, so the gate decision is identical.

WHY pass 3 still converges: anchor_moved fires whenever the LOD field could change; a generation bump fires when a finer neighbor arrives (that neighbor's Ready transition bumps it), which is exactly the missing_transition_faces / seam-repair trigger. So a dirty chunk or a moved anchor always re-runs the full candidate build — seam cracks and LOD demotions still converge. The only thing eliminated is the scan-and-find-nothing case on a quiescent world.

CLEANUP A (collision set): replace the O(N) pass-4 scan (:2247-2259) with a small std::vector<ChunkID> m_pending_collision drained per frame under the existing MAX_COLLISION_MESHES_PER_FRAME cap. A chunk is pushed when it becomes Ready at a renderable LOD0 mesh with has_collision==false (in process_completed_meshing_jobs and EnsureSurfaceReadyNear, right where has_collision.store(false) already happens). Drain front-to-back, re-defer entries still uncreated when the cap is hit. This removes the full scan even on the dirty path and makes collision creation order deterministic (insertion order, which is the deterministic Ready order).

CLEANUP B (telemetry dedup): the two identical state-count scans (pass 1 :1953-1972 and pass 5 :2263-2283) are pure telemetry into m_last_streaming_budget_stats (never hashed). Keep exactly ONE scan, at the END of update, so the stats reflect post-update state. On the elided (clean) frames, run only this single cheap count scan (or, cheaper, maintain running ready/renderable/idle/loading/meshing counters incremented at the same transition points and skip the scan entirely — optional second-stage optimization). This halves the telemetry cost on every frame and keeps stats live on elided frames (no frozen counters).

design.rationale: world_hash is computed by the server AFTER update() + wait_for_streaming_jobs() (ServerWorldRunner.cpp:394, :415-437), so it only ever reflects the quiesced result of work this update chose to dispatch. The elision gate is a pure function of replayed inputs: anchor_positions (replayed bit-identically; single-anchor forwards to {camera_position} at :1930) and m_streaming_state.dirty_generation, which is bumped only at deterministic state-transition points (Ready transitions, inserts, erases, edits) that already occur in identical order in run and replay. It depends on NOTHING excluded from the snapshot — no wall-clock, no render-thread mesh upload, no frame timing. Therefore run and replay take the SAME branch on every frame and dispatch the SAME meshing/collision work, so mesh_vertices/mesh_indices/has_collision/current_lod (the hashed fields, WorldPersistenceRoundtrip.cpp:29-56, 228-267) are identical at every snapshot. The activation cadence is preserved exactly because m_update_tick_counter++ and the update_chunk_activation gate are left untouched and the guard includes the `+1 >= INTERVAL` term so the activation frame always runs the full pass. Passes 1/5 and the new metrics/elided flag and m_last_anchor_positions/m_last_serviced_generation are telemetry/scratch state that is NEVER serialized or hashed. The collision set (cleanup A) only reorders WHICH frame a collider is created within the existing MAX_COLLISION_MESHES_PER_FRAME budget, in deterministic Ready insertion order, and has_collision still converges to true for every eligible chunk before the next hash (wait_for_streaming_jobs + repeated drains), so the quiesced hashed state is unchanged. red_team.verdict: NOT safe to implement as-is from the determinism lens — but the core gate is closer to correct than the design's own rationale claims. The premise survives the strongest determinism attacks I could mount: world_hash IS computed only after update()+wait_for_streaming_jobs() (ServerWorldRunner.cpp:385-394, :421) which runs process_completed_meshing_jobs() (SHIELD_WorldSystem.cpp:353), so the hash always reflects the quiesced result; and the hash is a pure FNV-1a over chunk JSON sorted by id (WorldPersistenceRoundtrip.cpp:311-318, 741-743), independent of iteration order, so the unordered_map traversal-order non-determinism cannot leak into it. As long as run and replay dispatch the SAME meshing/collision work, the post-quiesce hash matches. HOWEVER three things must be fixed before implementing: (1) the design's claim that mesh_version is NOT hashed is FALSE — mesh_version and water_mesh_version ARE hashed (WorldPersistenceRoundtrip.cpp:606, incremented at :3696/:3701/:2700), and pending_* fields and chunk state are hashed too, widening the surface the gate must keep bit-identical; (2) Cleanup A (collision set) changes WHICH frame has_collision flips from false→true, and has_collision IS hashed (:248) — this is only safe if quiescence guarantees every eligible chunk reaches has_collision==true before the hash, which the current per-frame MAX_COLLISION_MESHES_PER_FRAME cap does NOT guarantee (the existing scan is also capped, but the existing GATES never elide it and the existing carve/persistence test routes through EnsureSurfaceReadyNear which creates collision unconditionally, NOT through update()); (3) the anchor_moved chunk-cell threshold is mismatched to the actual LOD function, which keys off continuous Euclidean distance, not chunk cells.

objections.issue: FACTUAL ERROR in the design's hashed-field set undermines the gate's safety argument. The design states mesh_vertices/mesh_indices/has_collision/current_lod are the hashed fields and implies mesh_version is excluded. The actual world_hash (FNV-1a over ChunkToJson, WorldPersistenceRoundtrip.cpp:311-318, 235-259, validated at :593-606) ALSO hashes: mesh_version, water_mesh_version, water_mesh_generated, applied_transition_faces is NOT in the list but state/state_value ARE, and ALL pending_* fields (pending_mesh_vertices/indices/water/lod/ready/failed). mesh_version is bumped at SHIELD_WorldSystem.cpp:3696, :3701, :2700 — i.e. every applied remesh increments a HASHED counter. The gate only stays safe if the SAME set of remeshes happens in run and replay (which it does IFF the dispatch decision is a pure replayed-input function), but the design rationale is reasoning from an incomplete and partly-wrong field list, so the implementer cannot trust the stated invariant audit.
objections.mitigation: Before coding, re-derive the hashed surface from WorldPersistenceRoundtrip.cpp ChunkToJson (lines 215-260) — it is the ground truth, not the design's list. Restate the invariant as: 'on the dirty path run==replay dispatch identical meshing work in identical order, and on the clean path NEITHER run nor replay dispatch any, so mesh_version/pending_*/state are bit-identical at the next quiesce.' Add a gate assertion that on elided frames scheduled_meshing==0 AND no chunk's mesh_version/state changed.

objections.issue: Cleanup A (collision set) is the single biggest determinism risk and the design under-weights it. has_collision IS hashed (WorldPersistenceRoundtrip.cpp:248). Today's pass-4 scan (SHIELD_WorldSystem.cpp:2247-2259) is throttled by MAX_COLLISION_MESHES_PER_FRAME=16 (:23) but runs EVERY frame on the full chunk set, so on a many-chunk world it takes several frames to flip every eligible chunk to has_collision==true. The hash is computed after wait_for_streaming_jobs() (which does NOT create colliders — it only waits on gen/mesh jobs and calls process_completed_meshing_jobs, SHIELD_WorldSystem.cpp:3790-3793). Therefore at hash time some freshly-Ready chunks legitimately still have has_collision==false, and the hash captures that transient. Both run and replay reach the SAME transient TODAY only because the per-frame scan order is deterministic over the same chunk membership and the same per-frame budget. Replacing the scan with a drained m_pending_collision vector changes the ORDER and the SET of chunks that get colliders in a given frame (push order = Ready-transition order, which is meshing-completion order, NOT the unordered_map scan order). If the number of frames-to-quiesce differs by even one between run and replay, the has_collision bitfield at the snapshot frame differs and the hash diverges.
objections.mitigation: Do NOT change collision creation order/timing in the same change as the elision gate. Either (a) keep pass-4 EXACTLY as today (full scan, same order) and only gate it behind streaming_dirty — accepting the residual O(N) collision scan on dirty frames — OR (b) prove via the determinism gates (PopulatedWorldReplay/ReplayRoundtrip) that the snapshot frame is always reached AFTER full collision quiescence so has_collision is uniformly true and order is irrelevant. Verify the world-hash artifacts under build/debug/test-artifacts/persistence/ are byte-identical with Cleanup A IN vs OUT before trusting it.

objections.issue: anchor_moved threshold is mismatched to the real LOD function and can elide genuine LOD transitions. get_required_lod_for_chunk (SHIELD_WorldSystem.cpp:1786-1843) selects LOD from CONTINUOUS Euclidean distance glm::distance(camera, chunk_center) vs band thresholds m_lod_levels[].distance, with asymmetric hysteresis. The proposed anchor_moved gates on world_to_chunk_coords(a) delta (a 16 m chunk-cell crossing, design step 7 / open-question 1). An anchor moving <16 m (same chunk cell) can still cross a continuous LOD band edge for some chunk, flipping band_lod. With the cell-crossing gate, anchor_moved==false and dirty_generation unchanged, so the LOD remesh is ELIDED. In run==replay both elide identically (the gate stays GREEN), so this is NOT a hash divergence — but it IS a real LOD-correctness/visual regression: stale LOD and unrepaired seam cracks until the anchor finally crosses a full chunk cell. The design's own open-question 1 flags this but the steps bake in the wrong threshold anyway.
objections.mitigation: Gate anchor_moved on something at least as fine as the LOD decision. Cheapest deterministic option: quantize each anchor to a sub-chunk grid finer than the smallest LOD-band hysteresis margin (margin = CHUNK_SIZE_X = 16 m at :1835, but band edges are continuous), OR simply treat anchor_moved as true whenever any anchor's integer-quantized position (e.g. to 1 m) changed AND recompute is cheap. Safest: keep the full candidate loop whenever ANY anchor moved at all (even sub-cell), only eliding on a truly static anchor — which is the actual measured win case (static dense pose). Do not optimize the moving-camera path here.

objections.issue: dirty_generation is a CONSERVATIVE cover that depends on an exhaustive audit of every chunk-field writer, and the codebase already contains a writer OUTSIDE the listed transition points. RuntimeScenarioHarness.cpp:4807-4889 mutates chunk.sdf_data[index] directly and sets current_lod.store(-1) + mark_voxel_data_dirty() WITHOUT bumping dirty_generation. Any future per-frame voxel edit / mining / structure placement (FR-B1, recent commits e3c602d9) that mutates a chunk in place and relies on update()'s Ready-state candidate loop to remesh would be silently skipped on a clean frame, producing a missed remesh. Per the design's own caveat this stays replay-consistent (both runs miss identically) so gates stay GREEN — masking a real visual/gameplay bug that no determinism gate will catch.
objections.mitigation: Grep-audit every writer of sdf_data/material_data/current_lod/mesh_*/has_collision/has_water_sim/water_mesh_generated/applied_transition_faces and every caller of mark_voxel_data_dirty(); require each to bump dirty_generation. Add a debug-only assertion in update() that recomputes the full candidate set on a sampled cadence (e.g. every Nth elided frame) and aborts if it would have found work the gate claimed was clean — catches a missed bump in CI without costing the steady-state win.

objections.issue: The gate term `m_update_tick_counter + 1 >= STREAMING_ACTIVATION_INTERVAL_FRAMES` (design step 7) couples the elision decision to update_chunk_activation cadence, but update_chunk_activation itself MUTATES membership (erase at :2596, insert at :2651/:3451) which feeds passes 2-4. On the activation frame the design runs the full pass (correct), but on the 3 NON-activation frames between, if activation last added/removed chunks, dirty_generation must already be bumped by those insert/erase points (design steps 5-6 cover this). The ordering risk: process_completed_meshing_jobs runs at the TOP of update (:1935) and bumps dirty_generation, but m_last_serviced_generation is only updated at the END on the dirty branch (step 13). If a meshing job completes during wait_for_streaming_jobs() AFTER update() returned (server calls wait at :394, AFTER update), the Ready transition + bump happens there, and the NEXT update()'s top-of-frame process_completed_meshing_jobs may double-handle — need to confirm the bump-once-per-applied-chunk invariant holds across the update/wait boundary and is identical in run vs replay.
objections.mitigation: Ensure dirty_generation is bumped inside process_completed_meshing_jobs exactly once per chunk whose results are APPLIED (guard on the mesh_ready branch at :3678-3703), never on the early-return-no-jobs path (:3664-3666). Confirm wait_for_streaming_jobs()->wait_for_meshing_jobs()->process_completed_meshing_jobs() (:3792) runs the SAME apply+bump in run and replay (it does — it is pure over job outputs which are pure over replayed inputs). Add a gate check that dirty_generation advances identically across a recorded run and its replay.

objections.issue: Telemetry dedup (Cleanup B) and the new render-benchmark v3 schema are out-of-scope risk surface. m_last_streaming_budget_stats feeds downstream consumers; the design adds 5 new fields and bumps schema to v3 (steps 3, 15). queue_depth at :2285 is derived from terrain_meshing_backlog which is only computed on the dirty branch — on elided frames terrain_meshing_backlog==0, so last_queue_depth and the settled-floor ring (:2285-2294) would read artificially 0 on every clean frame, corrupting the EnduranceStreamDrain/queue-depth telemetry and any gate keyed on peak_queue_depth.

Confirm no determinism gate consumes m_last_streaming_budget_stats (it is telemetry, not hashed — verified, stats are never serialized into world_hash). Keep schema-v3 strictly additive and confirm no CI parser hard-codes v2.

must_fix: Re-derive the hashed-field set from WorldPersistenceRoundtrip.cpp ChunkToJson (lines 215-260) — mesh_version, water_mesh_version, pending_* and chunk state/state_value ARE hashed; the design's claim that mesh_version is excluded is wrong and its invariant audit is built on that wrong list.

red_team.verdict: NOT safe to implement as-is. The elision gate has one BLOCKING determinism/correctness hole: the deterministic dirty signals it lists do NOT include the chunk Idle transition produced by generation jobs (SHIELD_WorldSystem.cpp:3458 and the GPU-SDF path :3305), which is the ONLY producer of the meshing candidates the candidate loop consumes (the loop's Idle->needs_meshing branch at :2093 is the sole Idle->Meshing path). That transition happens on a background worker thread and the design's own gate term that is supposed to cover in-flight generation (has_active_job(generation_job_handle)) reads false on the exact frame the work lands, because has_active_job (:258-260) returns counter>0 and the counter has already decremented to 0 by the time the main thread observes the now-Idle chunks; clear_completed_job_handle (:1934) then nulls the handle at the top of the next update. Result: on a non-activation frame an Idle chunk can satisfy NONE of the dirty terms, so passes 2-3 are skipped and the chunk is not dispatched to meshing until up to STREAMING_ACTIVATION_INTERVAL_FRAMES (=4, :33) ticks later. In the current code passes 2-3 run EVERY frame, so the Idle chunk meshes on the very next update(); the elision therefore SHIFTS the tick on which a chunk's mesh_vertices/mesh_indices/current_lod (hashed fields) first appear. Because the replay gates capture mid-run world_hash checkpoints (ServerWorldRunner ComputeWorldHashAndSubHashes, each after wait_for_streaming_jobs which waits-but-does-not-remesh, :394/:495), a checkpoint landing in that 1-4 tick window will mismatch the pinned baseline -> PopulatedWorldReplay / ReplayRoundtrip RED. This is not merely a convergence-latency issue; it changes the per-tick hashed-state trajectory and the gate decision itself depends on worker-thread timing (an input excluded from the snapshot), so run vs replay can even take different branches. Two additional medium issues (sub-cell LOD-band crossing missed by the chunk-cell anchor_moved threshold; collision-set staleness when a chunk is re-meshed/erased) need fixing before this is shippable. The structural cleanups (telemetry dedup, collision set) are sound in principle.

objections.issue: GENERATION->IDLE TRANSITION IS NOT A DIRTY-BUMP POINT AND IS NOT COVERED BY THE GATE. The candidate loop's only Idle-source is generation jobs completing on worker threads (SHIELD_WorldSystem.cpp:3458 set_state(Idle), and the GPU-SDF path :3305). The design bumps dirty_generation at meshing-completion (:3703/05/07), EnsureSurfaceReadyNear (:2702), inserts (:2651/:3451/:3816) and erase (:2596) -- but NOT at the gen-job Idle transition. The intended safety net, has_active_job(generation_job_handle), fails on the landing frame: has_active_job (:258) is counter>0, the worker decrements the counter to 0 and sets the chunk Idle BEFORE the next main-thread update observes it, and clear_completed_job_handle (:1934) then resets the handle. So on a non-activation, non-anchor-moved frame, a freshly-Idle chunk matches NO dirty term and passes 2-3 are elided. Today (passes 2-3 every frame) that chunk meshes on the next update(); under the gate it stalls up to STREAMING_ACTIVATION_INTERVAL_FRAMES=4 ticks (:33,:1990). On the server, update_chunk_activation dispatches generation on the activation tick (counter reset to 0, :1992); the resulting Idle chunks therefore appear right after an activation tick and must wait ~4 ticks for the +1>=INTERVAL term to re-run the full pass. This both delays meshing and makes the gate decision a function of worker-thread completion timing -- an input excluded from the world snapshot.
objections.mitigation: Add an explicit deterministic bump that fires when a generation job's result is consumed on the MAIN thread, not on the worker. Cleanest: bump dirty_generation inside update() right after clear_completed_job_handle/process_completed_meshing_jobs whenever the generation handle just transitioned active->inactive (track m_gen_was_active last frame; on the falling edge, force one dirty pass). Equivalently keep streaming_dirty=true for the frame after ANY generation handle was active, OR maintain a deterministic main-thread-observed Idle counter (a uint64 bumped when update() first sees a chunk in Idle that it hasn't serviced). Whatever the mechanism, the dirty signal MUST be derived from main-thread observation of chunk state, never from has_active_job's race-prone counter. Re-verify that an Idle chunk is meshed on the SAME tick as baseline (diff per-tick world_hash, not just end-state).

objections.issue: PASS-2 meshed_columns / seam-repair input depends on a NEIGHBOR's late mesh arrival, which is itself a meshing-completion event -- covered by a bump -- BUT only if the coarse chunk and its finer neighbor are serviced in the SAME or a later dirty frame. The seam-crack trigger (missing_transition_faces, :2043-2063, fed by meshed_columns built at :2027) fires when a finer neighbor arrives after a coarse chunk was meshed. The finer neighbor's Ready transition bumps dirty_generation (:3703), so the next frame is dirty and the coarse chunk re-runs the candidate loop -- GOOD. However, if the coarse chunk's required_lod did not change and the ONLY reason to remesh is the seam, and the dirty frame that processed the neighbor's arrival ALSO hit the meshing_job_active early-out (:2201 guards dispatch on !meshing_job_active), the seam remesh is deferred to a later frame; if dirty_generation is cleared (m_last_serviced_generation updated at end of that dirty frame, design step :2323) before the seam remesh actually dispatched, a subsequent settled frame will NOT re-attempt it and the crack persists until the next unrelated dirty event.
objections.mitigation: Do NOT advance m_last_serviced_generation when the dirty pass did not fully drain its intended work (i.e. when meshing_job_active blocked dispatch, or candidates were deferred over budget at :2237). Only mark serviced when meshing_candidates was built AND (empty OR fully dispatched with zero deferred). Simpler and safer: gate m_last_serviced_generation=dirty_generation on (deferred_meshing==0 && !meshing_jobs_active()). This keeps the world dirty until the meshing pipeline is genuinely quiescent, matching the server's per-tick wait_for_streaming_jobs quiesce assumption.

objections.issue: COLLISION SET (Cleanup A) CAN GO STALE / MISS, causing player fall-through. m_pending_collision is push-only at Ready transitions (:3697 has_collision.store(false) and :2701). But (a) a chunk that is RE-MESHED (LOD promotion to 0, or seam remesh) sets has_collision.store(false) again at :3697 -- the design pushes there, OK -- yet if that chunk's id is already drained/removed from m_pending_collision and then re-meshed, it must be RE-pushed; the predicate 'became Ready with LOD0 && !has_collision' must be evaluated on EVERY mesh application, not only first Ready. (b) A chunk erased (:2596) while still in m_pending_collision leaves a dangling id; the drain's find() handles that, OK. (c) The original scan (:2247) re-checks current_lod==0 LIVE each frame, so a chunk meshed at LOD1 then promoted to LOD0 was naturally picked up; the set must capture the LOD0-promotion specifically. If any has_collision.store(false) site is missed in the push instrumentation, that chunk NEVER gets a collider (the full scan that would have caught it is gone) -> permanent fall-through on newly streamed/promoted ground.
objections.mitigation: Push to m_pending_collision at EVERY site that does has_collision.store(false) (audit: :2701, :3697, and any future remesh path), unconditionally, and let the drain's live predicate (state==Ready && current_lod==0 && mesh non-empty && !has_collision) decide eligibility -- never pre-filter on push. De-dup with a small membership set if a chunk can be pushed twice before draining. Add a CHEAP periodic full-scan safety net (e.g. only on the activation tick, every 4 frames) as a backstop so a single missed push self-heals within one interval instead of becoming permanent. Verify with the design's own fall-through walk test AND a LOD1->LOD0 promotion-into-collision test.

objections.issue: anchor_moved CHUNK-CELL THRESHOLD MISSES SUB-CELL LOD-BAND CROSSINGS. get_required_lod_for_chunk (:1808-1818) computes LOD from continuous glm::distance with band thresholds (>=192 m) and a 16 m hysteresis margin. The proposed anchor_moved fires only when world_to_chunk_coords delta != 0 (a 16 m cell crossing). An anchor drifting WITHIN one 16 m cell can still move a chunk's distance across a band boundary (e.g. 191 m -> 193 m), changing required_lod, without tripping anchor_moved. On a moving anchor this delays a legitimate LOD demotion/promotion (visible LOD pop / transient seam) until the next cell crossing or unrelated dirty event.
objections.mitigation: This only matters on a moving anchor (the target optimization is the STATIC case, where it is moot). Either accept the bounded one-cell-of-travel lag (the existing hysteresis already tolerates a chunk of travel) OR, to be safe, force streaming_dirty whenever any anchor is within K cells of a band-distance boundary, OR quantize the anchor on a finer grid than 16 m for the comparison. Confirm via the design's moving-camera convergence check that no persistent LOD crack appears at band edges during slow drift.

objections.issue: pending_lod>=0 CHUNKS AND meshing_jobs_active EARLY-OUT INTERACTION. The candidate loop skips chunks with pending_lod>=0 (:2074-2077) and dispatch is blocked while meshing_jobs_active (:2201). A chunk can be mid-flight (pending_lod set) across the boundary between a dirty frame and a clean frame. If the meshing job completes on a clean (elided) frame, process_completed_meshing_jobs (:1935, always runs) bumps dirty_generation at :3703 -- GOOD, the next frame is dirty. But if m_last_serviced_generation was advanced on the prior dirty frame and the completion bump lands, the comparison dirty_generation != m_last_serviced_generation correctly re-fires. This is OK ONLY because process_completed_meshing_jobs is unconditionally called before the gate. Confirm the gate is computed strictly AFTER process_completed_meshing_jobs (design step :1933-1952 says so) -- if any refactor moves the gate before it, completed-mesh follow-on remeshes (seam repair seeded by the just-applied finer LOD) would be missed for a frame.
objections.mitigation: Keep process_completed_meshing_jobs() strictly before the gate computation (assert ordering in a comment/test). The design already places it correctly; flag it as load-bearing so a later edit does not reorder it.

objections.issue: WATER REMESH PATH (water_mesh_generated) IS A NON-LOD DIRTY TRIGGER NOT TIED TO A GENERATION/READY TRANSITION. The candidate loop triggers a (terrain-mesh-not-required) remesh when required_lod==0 && has_water_sim && !water_mesh_generated (:2106-2111). has_water_sim / water_mesh_generated are set by the water system update (m_water_system->update at :1998, which runs every frame OUTSIDE the gate) and by mesh application (:3620). A frame where the water system flips has_water_sim true on an already-Ready, settled chunk (no anchor move, no gen, no mesh completion) would NOT bump dirty_generation, so the water remesh is elided.
objections.mitigation: Have the water system path bump dirty_generation (or set a dedicated water-dirty flag folded into streaming_dirty) whenever it newly sets has_water_sim/clears water_mesh_generated on a chunk. Since m_water_system->update already runs every frame, capture whether it changed any chunk's water flags and OR that into streaming_dirty for the frame. Verify a chunk that gains water sim on a static anchor still gets its water mesh.

must_fix: Add a deterministic, MAIN-THREAD-observed dirty signal for the generation-job Idle transition (SHIELD_WorldSystem.cpp:3458, :3305). The current gate term has_active_job(generation_job_handle) (:258, cleared at :1934) races worker-thread completion and reads false on the landing frame, so freshly-Idle chunks are elided from passes 2-3 and meshing is delayed up to STREAMING_ACTIVATION_INTERVAL_FRAMES (=4) ticks. Detect the generation-handle active->inactive falling edge on the main thread (or count main-thread-observed Idle chunks) and force a dirty pass. Re-verify by diffing PER-TICK world_hash (not just end-state) against baseline.

Do not advance m_last_serviced_generation / m_last_anchor_positions (design step :2323) on a dirty frame whose meshing work did not fully drain. Gate the advance on (deferred_meshing==0 && !meshing_jobs_active()) so a budget-deferred or job-blocked seam/LOD remesh is retried on the next frame instead of being abandoned until the next unrelated dirty event (otherwise persistent LOD seam cracks, :2043/:2201/:2237).

Make collision tracking robust: push to m_pending_collision at EVERY has_collision.store(false) site (audit :2701, :3697 and any remesh path) unconditionally, let the drain's live predicate filter, and add a cheap activation-tick full-scan backstop so a missed push self-heals within one interval. A single missed push under the removed full scan (:2247) is a permanent player fall-through.

Fold the water-remesh trigger into the dirty gate: when m_water_system->update (:1998) newly sets has_water_sim / clears water_mesh_generated on a settled chunk, OR that into streaming_dirty (the :2106 candidate branch is otherwise elided on a static anchor).

Verify determinism gates by diffing the PINNED per-tick world_hash baselines, not only confirming green: run HeadlessServerTick, PopulatedWorldReplay, ReplayRoundtrip, LockstepLoopback, NetworkedSession, LockstepFaultInjection AND byte-compare build/debug/test-artifacts/persistence/*.json against pre-change. Any per-tick checkpoint mismatch (even if end-state converges) means the elision shifted the hashed-state trajectory and must be reworked, not re-pinned.

red_team.verdict: From the VISUAL/GATES lens the design is SAFE TO IMPLEMENT with conditions, NOT safe as-is. The forest budget gate (FarFieldForestBudget) is a pure CPU harness (test/rendering/forest_perf_budget_test.cpp) that never touches SHIELD_WorldSystem::update — it is immune to the elision. The single-frame visual gates that pin a FIXED camera (LodGround, water/material/skybox/weather) are protected because they call EnsureSurfaceReadyNear SYNCHRONOUSLY every frame (main_client.cpp:3526) which bumps dirty_generation and forces the full pass, so the elided clean frame only ever happens once the world is already fully ready. The two REAL exposures are (1) PlayerView and FarLodHorizon, whose far field is streamed ONLY by the async per-frame update() at main_client.cpp:4540 during a multi-second FIXED-camera station hold (these branches at :4152/:4188 do NOT call EnsureSurfaceReadyNear), and (2) the WorldVisualSweep, which by its own comment (main_client.cpp:4977) deliberately relies on update() doing real streaming for exactly 24 warmup frames at a fixed anchor. In both, the camera anchor does not cross a chunk cell, so anchor_moved() is false and convergence rests entirely on the meshing_jobs_active()/dirty_generation chain plus the preserved activation cadence — which DOES converge in principle, but only if (a) every far-field chunk insert/Ready/LOD writer bumps dirty_generation (the design's own load-bearing open question) and (b) the station/warmup hold is long enough for the activation→dispatch→complete→re-dispatch chain to fully drain BEFORE the capture fires. Neither is verified by the proposed gate, and a single missed bump or a too-short warmup surfaces as a far-field hole / LOD seam in exactly the frame these visual baselines diff. The fix is cheap (verify-only, plus one belt-and-suspenders), so I require it before implementing rather than blocking the design.

objections.issue: PlayerView and FarLodHorizon gates stream their FAR field exclusively through the async per-frame update() (main_client.cpp:4540). Their per-station camera is held FIXED for the whole settle window (main_client.cpp:4152-4187 / 4188-4235 call ApplyPlayerViewCamera/ApplyFarLodHorizonCamera but NEVER EnsureSurfaceReadyNear — only LodGround does, at :3526). With a fixed sub-chunk camera, the proposed anchor_moved() (chunk-cell-crossing granularity, per step 7 and open_question 1) returns false. So far-field convergence during the hold depends entirely on the meshing_jobs_active()||dirty_generation chain firing every activation cycle. If the warmup/station window is even slightly shorter than the full activation(every 4 frames)→generate→mesh→apply→re-dispatch drain, the capture at 70% progress (player_view) or the phase-B sweep (farlod) shows a far-field hole / unfilled horizon ring that the all-real-geometry baseline did not have. The current code converges because the full candidate pass runs UNCONDITIONALLY every frame and re-scans the whole chunk set; the elision removes that safety margin and makes convergence timing-sensitive to the dirty_generation bump completeness.
objections.mitigation: Add an explicit gate-level guard to the verification plan: run player_view_smoke AND farlod_horizon_smoke (release AND debug) and pixel-diff the captured horizon/far-field band against the pre-change baseline — they MUST be byte/threshold-identical, not just 'green'. Additionally, as a belt-and-suspenders that costs nothing on a settled world, force streaming_dirty=true while get_renderable_chunks() count is still rising vs the previous frame (a cheap monotonic 'far field still growing' signal) so the warmup window can never elide before the far ring stops growing. Do NOT ship until both gates' far-field bands match baseline.

objections.issue: WorldVisualSweep EXPLICITLY depends on update() doing real streaming work for 24 warmup frames at a FIXED anchor (main_client.cpp:4977-4990: 'We stream for a bounded warmup... the same settled geometry is reused for every subsequent cell'). The anchor is g_camera->Position held constant, so anchor_moved() is false for all 24 frames. After the world first quiesces (no jobs active, dirty_generation matched, activation tick not due), the guard ELIDES — but the sweep's contract assumes 24 full update() passes complete the stream. If quiescence is reached at frame N<24 but a late activation cycle (every 4th frame) would still have pulled in a far rim chunk, the guard could skip the activation-triggered candidate pass on a clean frame and the sweep captures its whole 48-cell matrix against an under-streamed world — a missing-chunk regression across EVERY sweep cell at once.
objections.mitigation: The guard's '+1 >= STREAMING_ACTIVATION_INTERVAL_FRAMES' term (step 7) preserves the activation cadence, and update_chunk_activation inserts must bump dirty_generation (design step for inserts at :2651/:3451/:3816 — but verify the activation-path insert inside update_chunk_activation at the add_candidate/generation-dispatch site is covered, NOT just EnsureSurfaceReadyNear's insert). Concretely: confirm the generation-job completion that inserts newly-generated far chunks bumps dirty_generation, otherwise the frame after activation elides and the new chunks never get meshed. Add a sweep-specific verification: run world_visual_sweep and confirm every cell's chunk/foliage presence check (RunWorldVisualSweep already asserts presence) stays green, and diff at least the first and a far-looking cell PPM against baseline.

objections.issue: anchor_moved() at chunk-cell granularity (open_question 1) elides sub-chunk LOD-band changes. get_required_lod_for_chunk uses asymmetric hysteresis bands (SHIELD_WorldSystem.cpp:2099 with the meshed-LOD argument). A camera that pans/dollies WITHIN one chunk cell across a hysteresis band boundary changes the required LOD of distant chunks WITHOUT crossing a cell and WITHOUT a dirty_generation bump (no Ready/insert/erase/edit occurred). The full candidate pass that would detect required_lod != current_lod (SHIELD_WorldSystem.cpp:2103) is elided, so a visible LOD demotion/promotion (and any seam-skirt repair it implies) is silently skipped. In player_view's eye-level 360 sweep and the sweep matrix this manifests as a stale LOD / visible seam crack at distance in the captured frame versus baseline.
objections.mitigation: Resolve open_question 1 BEFORE coding, not after: audit get_required_lod_for_chunk to prove no LOD band boundary can be crossed by sub-chunk-cell anchor motion for any chunk in render range; if any can (likely, since bands are distance-in-metres not chunk-quantised), make anchor_moved() fire on a finer deterministic quantum (e.g. quantise anchor to the smallest band-width/2 in metres, still integer/deterministic) OR always-run when within K cells of a band boundary. The visual gates that MOVE the camera continuously (lod_boundary_oscillation_smoke, lod_seam_arrival_smoke — both in the :5016/:4537 lists) are the ones that will catch this; add them to the mandatory pre-merge gate set.

objections.issue: The collision-set cleanup (CLEANUP A) changes WHICH frame a collider is created and the foliage/grass scatter and FarLod readback paths key off get_renderable_chunks() (main_client.cpp:5143) and per-chunk Ready state every frame. The design gates the collision drain on 'streaming_dirty || !m_pending_collision.empty()' (step 11), which is fine, but if a chunk becomes Ready on an elided clean frame path (it shouldn't, because Ready transitions only happen in process_completed_meshing_jobs which runs BEFORE the guard and bumps dirty_generation), a renderable chunk could exist that the foliage rebuild sees but whose collider is deferred. This is not a visual-gate failure per se, but FoliageInstancing's foliage_visual_smoke rebuilds scatter over get_renderable_chunks() and asserts instance_hash/coverage — if the renderable set on the captured frame differs by even one chunk from baseline (because a candidate pass that would have remeshed a seam was elided), the foliage coverage hash diverges.
objections.mitigation: Because process_completed_meshing_jobs runs at the TOP of update() (SHIELD_WorldSystem.cpp:1935) before the guard, and the design bumps dirty_generation on every Ready transition there, the renderable set is stable across an elided frame BY CONSTRUCTION — verify this invariant holds by asserting get_renderable_chunks().size() is identical on an elided frame vs the prior frame in the new v3 telemetry. Run foliage_visual_smoke (FoliageInstancing) and confirm instance_hash/coverage match baseline. Low residual risk if the Ready-transition bump is complete.

objections.issue: The new render-benchmark schema bump to v3 (step 15) adds streaming_pass_elided + work-count fields. The visual/budget gates and any dashboard/CI parser that reads the render-benchmark or render-health JSON (build/debug/test-artifacts/render/render-health-analysis.json is already in the working tree as modified) may hard-code v2. A schema mismatch could fail the budget gate parse rather than the elision itself — a false-RED that masks whether the elision is actually safe.
objections.mitigation: Per open_question 5: grep all consumers of the render-benchmark/render-health schema version string before bumping, and bump every reader in the same change. Keep the v3 fields PURELY ADDITIVE (the design says they are) so a v2 reader that ignores unknown keys still parses. Confirm the FarFieldForestBudget validator (-Mode FarFieldForestBudget) reads forest_perf_budget.json (schema v1, untouched) and is unaffected.

objections.issue: No visual gate exercises a STATIC fully-settled in-world camera with the per-frame update() as the ONLY streaming driver AND then verifies geometry presence — that is precisely the elision's target case, and it is the render-benchmark (--render-benchmark, scenario-LESS, main_client.cpp:3039/g_render_benchmark_path) which has NO presence/pixel assertion, only GPU timers. So the one configuration the optimization most changes is measured for SPEED but not for CORRECTNESS (missing chunks). A regression where the elision drops a late far chunk on a static camera would show as a FASTER benchmark (good number) with a hole in the unmeasured frame.
objections.mitigation: Add the render-benchmark-screenshot (g_render_benchmark_screenshot, main_client.cpp:168) to the verification: capture the dense static pose PPM with the elision ON and pixel-diff against the same pose with the elision forced OFF (a debug env flag to disable the guard). They MUST match within the visual threshold. This is the only way to prove 'faster' did not mean 'emptier'. Pair it with the static-camera work-count assertion already in the plan (streaming_pass_elided==true on steady frames) so you prove BOTH that it elided AND that the picture is unchanged.

must_fix: Add player_view_smoke and farlod_horizon_smoke to the MANDATORY pre-merge gate set and pixel-diff their far-field/horizon bands against the pre-change baseline (not just 'green') — these stream the far field ONLY via the elided update() at a fixed sub-chunk camera (main_client.cpp:4152/4188, no EnsureSurfaceReadyNear), so they are the primary regression surface.

Add a render-benchmark-screenshot pixel-diff of the dense STATIC pose: elision ON vs elision forced-OFF must match within the visual threshold. The plain --render-benchmark measures GPU ms only and would report a hole as a FASTER frame; without a pixel check 'faster' is indistinguishable from 'emptier'.

Resolve open_question 1 (anchor_moved granularity vs get_required_lod_for_chunk hysteresis bands at SHIELD_WorldSystem.cpp:2099) BEFORE coding: prove no LOD band boundary is crossable by sub-chunk-cell anchor motion in render range, or make anchor_moved fire on a finer deterministic quantum. Add lod_boundary_oscillation_smoke + lod_seam_arrival_smoke to the gate set to catch a stale-LOD seam.

Prove the far-field/activation insert path bumps dirty_generation: the generation-job completion that inserts newly-generated far chunks (via update_chunk_activation at SHIELD_WorldSystem.cpp:2325+) must bump, not only EnsureSurfaceReadyNear's insert at :2651. A missed bump there lets the frame after a 4-frame activation cycle elide and the new far chunks never mesh — exactly what WorldVisualSweep (24-frame fixed-anchor warmup, main_client.cpp:4977) and the station holds depend on.

Add a cheap monotonic safety net: force streaming_dirty=true while get_renderable_chunks() count is still increasing vs the previous frame, so no warmup/station hold can elide before the far ring stops growing — removes the timing-sensitivity of the convergence chain at near-zero steady-state cost.

Run FoliageInstancing's foliage_visual_smoke and assert get_renderable_chunks().size() is identical on an elided frame vs the prior frame (new v3 telemetry), so the foliage scatter coverage/instance_hash that keys off the renderable set (main_client.cpp:5143) cannot diverge from baseline.
